bullets.text: MEASURED: the ground_loop process started 2026-08-13 15:35:43. Commit ba50814 ('the big bang: 24 components drop one level into their rungs') moved cairn/base/probe.py to cairn/tools/base/probe.py at 20:55 the same evening. For the 29 hours between then and now, fifteen devices carrying twenty-two probes were skipped by the heartbeat.

THE MECHANISM, and it is ordinary Python: discovery.load_module execs each probe file off its path, so the probe binds the CURRENT cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe, while the daemon's own frame still held cairn.base.probe.Probe from before the move. Two distinct class objects wearing one name. isinstance() is an identity test, so it returned False, and the loop reported 'PROBE is Probe, not a Probe' thirteen times.

The two remaining faces are the same staleness from the other side: constrain and orient failed with ImportError for common_shape_record and AmbiguousComponent, both symbols added to cairn.tools.chain.grammar AFTER the process started. One root cause, two error classes, and neither of them names the loop.

THE BENCH MADE IT SELF-SEALING. A benched device is passed to discover() in skip, so it is never re-scanned, its trouble stops recurring, and its count freezes. Four tickets sat at ~10,286 occurrences with last_seen 23.7 hours old — which reads as an outage that ended. It had not ended; it had gone total. An outage that stops recurring is indistinguishable from one that was fixed.

A RESTART ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT, which is the trap for whoever meets this next. loop.py:50 defines the bench as 'a live ticket by this name exists', and clearing is the recipient's act alone — so a restarted loop keeps every device dark, silently, with the imports now perfectly fine and nothing red anywhere. The order is restart, verify through the loop's own discover(), then clear.

The predicate that was missing is one comparison and every input to it is already free on disk: is this process older than the code it is judging. Process start time, file mtimes, and the module file behind a class object are all readable, and the check only ever runs on the failure path — so a healthy system pays nothing for it.

For Akien, and it is the part I am least comfortable with: I READ THIS TROUBLE LIST AT SESSION OPEN AND WALKED PAST IT. So did every session before this one. It took building a probe of my own, watching it get benched within a minute, and refusing to accept the message at face value. The list was loud, correctly recorded, and pointed at the wrong party — and being pointed at the wrong party is what made it quiet.

FOUND ONLY BY UN-BENCHING and owed its own ticket, recorded here so it cannot be re-derived: with the watch layer actually armed, probe triggers cost 2531 ms per beat over 22 probes (build_inspector 705, base 1170 across five, inference_domain 566). The beat slowed to ~3.5s against the ruled 5s liveness threshold, so a healthy loop now reads DEAD about a third of the time. The heartbeat had been cheap for 29 hours because it was doing nothing.

AN INSTRUMENT CANNOT AUDIT WHAT IT SITS UPSTREAM OF. bullets.text: THE PARENT IS SHORT A CHILD, and it is Akien's own second named example. every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree carries FIVE falsifier clauses and FOUR children, and clause (3) — 'a probe firing at a gate crossing leaves one' — is owned by none of them. Measured at cairn/tools/base/shim.py:74: `class BaseShim(CoreValuesMixin, ABC)`, no DiagnosticBase in the bases, so the component that fires probes has no emit() at all. Child (1) closed the wiring for DEVICES and structurally could not reach this, because a shim is not a device. The parent cannot honestly cross PROVED against a falsifier one of whose clauses no child owns — and the fix is likely one line in the bases, which is what makes the gap worth naming now rather than at the parent's crossing.

ONE MISSING SHAPE BLOCKS BOTH ROADS, which is why the floor and not the device is where this child builds. inference_domain cannot emit because it has NO CLASS (domain.py, host.py, route.py are modules of functions — measured: zero emit sites, and not from oversight); BaseShim cannot emit because its class does not carry the mixin. Both reduce to 'a component that is not a BaseDevice has no way to reach its own trail'. The floor answer this child builds — a trail scoped to a MODULE address rather than a class address, deriving its device name through the same address.component_of_module the class side uses — is the same answer clause (3) needs.

THE ASSUMPTION THAT DIED DURING THE COMPLETENESS CHECK, recorded because it makes the claim smaller and truer. I had taken it that BreadcrumbLog was reachable only through DiagnosticBase, which would have made the floor work mandatory before anything could log. It is not — BreadcrumbLog(device, instance) is a plain constructor and any module can build one and hand it a record TODAY, with no new code. So the floor seam is not load-bearing for 'can a module log at all'; it is load-bearing for 'is there exactly ONE author of the record shape', since the shape (ts/us/source/gate/pointer/values/home) is built inside DiagnosticBase.emit and a second author is a second thing to keep in step with the inspector that reads it.

THE GRAIN DECISION, made at this cast rather than left to the build: ONE record per inference call at the outcome, carrying the host that answered and the rungs walked past as a VALUE on that record — never one record per rung. /intent left these in unnoticed tension (its falsifier wanted 'which host answered', its wrong-intent clause forbade a record per rung), and host.py's resolver WALKS rungs cheapest-first on HostUnreachable, so the two collide in the ordinary case. A walk is one crossing with a path, not three crossings. This keeps an ordinary cheapest-first resolution from reading as three failures while still answering 'why was it slow'.

A CACHE HIT IS A BOUNDARY NOT CROSSED, and saying so is what turns this trail from present into useful. The domain already keeps a meter (yield_report: tokens SPENT on misses against tokens AVOIDED by hits), so the trail will describe the same events a store already describes — a Law 7 exposure rather than a redundancy. The falsifier and the watch are both built on that: they ask the two records to AGREE over a window, which is also the only clause of this proof whose evidence the proof cannot write both halves of, since the store side is written by resolve()'s existing path.

A DISTINCTION THE FLOOR'S CHARTER DOES NOT YET DRAW, owed as a charter delta by this build. diagnostic.py's discipline paragraph says instrumentation is 'targeted and TEMPORARY... not standing probes left hanging', which was written when home was an in-memory mailbox and the risk was flooding a live process. Home is a file now, swept at 30 days. There are two legitimate acts and the file names only one: a TARGETED instrument placed to catch a specific flake and then taken down, and a STANDING trail at a named boundary — which is what Akien's brief asks for ('every single everyting is supposed to log major boundry crossings'). The bound that survives from that paragraph is the GRAIN, not the duration.
